metadata.title: 16-bit or 24-bit: What Bit Depth Does
metadata.note: Audio-concept explainer: bit depth, for someone who has never opened an audio editor. Through-line: bit depth is ROOM TO WORK IN, not quality. ONE measured pair of numbers only (−53 dB at 8-bit, −101 dB at 16-bit) — see MEASUREMENTS.txt, measured in float64 numpy because ffmpeg's filter graph is 32-bit float internally and cannot measure 24-bit at all. WRITTEN FOR A COMPLETE BEGINNER. Beat 1 is a BACKGROUND beat that starts from what sound even is and shows where the viewer meets this setting; beat 2 leads with an everyday ANALOGY before any mechanism. No jargon survives without a plain-language definition in the same sentence. Balance, not dumbing down: the viewer should finish able to make the decision themselves. WORD-CLOCK CHOREOGRAPHED via cues.json + sync_cues.py — every reveal lands on a measured spoken phrase, never a guessed fraction. TYPOGRAPHY: Source Serif 4 + Inter loaded via @remotion/google-fonts. beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Row-Haan, for Humanitarians AI. Save a recording on almost any device and something will ask you a question: sixteen bit, or twenty-four? No explanation. No default that is obviously right. By the end of this you'll know exactly what that number controls, and which one to pick.

props.command: My export box is asking for 16-bit or 24-bit. What does that number actually control?
output: sound becomes a list of numbers
bit depth = how precisely each one is written
24 to work in, 16 to send out

beats.narration_text: Start with what sound actually is. It's movement — air pressure rising and falling. A microphone feels that movement, and a computer has to write it down as a list of numbers. To do that, it answers two separate questions. How often should I take a measurement? That's called the sample rate. And how precisely should I write each measurement down? That's bit depth. Today we only care about the second one.

props.title: How Sound Becomes A File
props.sparkLine: Two questions. This video is the second one.

beats.narration_text: Think of a ruler. A ruler marked only in centimetres and a ruler marked in millimetres are the same length — one just lets you be more precise. Bit depth is how many markings your ruler has. And here's the catch: every measurement has to land exactly on a marking. Anything in between gets pushed to the nearest one.

props.title: A Ruler, And What It Cannot Measure
props.sparkLine: Everything lands on a marking, or gets pushed to one.

beats.narration_text: So every stored number is slightly off. Tiny on its own — but this happens tens of thousands of times every second, and all those little errors together add up to a sound of their own. A faint hiss, sitting underneath your music. And the coarser your ruler, the bigger each error, and the louder that hiss.

props.title: All Those Small Errors Are A Sound

beats.narration_text: Here's what that is actually worth. At eight bits, the hiss sits about fifty decibels below full volume. At sixteen bits, about a hundred. And a hundred decibels is roughly the gap between a whisper and a rock concert. So at sixteen bits the hiss is already quieter than the room you are sitting in right now. You will never hear it.

props.title: How Much Quiet You Actually Get

rows.label: 8-bit
rows.note: hiss is audible in quiet passages

rows.label: 16-bit
rows.note: hiss is below any real room

props.anchor: ≈ 100 dB is a whisper to a rock concert
props.footnote: Measured in float64 numpy against the unquantised original. ffmpeg's filter graph is 32-bit float internally, so it cannot measure 24-bit at all.
props.sparkLine: At 16 bits you will never hear the bottom.

beats.narration_text: So why does twenty-four exist? Because while you are working, every edit rounds all over again. Turn something up, and you turn its hiss up with it. Twenty-four bit gives you room to absorb all of that. So record and edit in twenty-four. Export in sixteen. Your listener gains nothing from more.

props.title: Which One To Pick
props.lede: 24-bit to work in. 16-bit to send out.
steps: Recording and editing: 24-bit. Every edit rounds again, and you want room to absorb it.
Sending to listeners: 16-bit. The hiss is already below any real room, and the file is a third smaller.
Never save down to 16 and then keep editing — the hiss you added does not come back out.
props.sparkLine: Keep the room while you work. Spend it when you ship.

beats.narration_text: Bit depth isn't quality. It's room to work in. Keep it while you edit, spend it when you ship. I'm Row-Haan VeeJayKooMaar, for Humanitarians AI.
